name: MARCO INKMAN
bio:
In the world of black-and-grey realism, Marco Inkman stands out for his balance, precision, and narrative depth. His style, deeply influenced by Chicano art, is the result of a long artistic and personal journey that has shaped his clear vision of tattooing as a living and culturally rooted form of expression. After building a strong reputation in Italy, Marco made the decision in 2021 to leave Montecchio Maggiore behind and pursue an international career as a guest artist. Since then, he has worked regularly in some of the most respected studios around the world, traveling between Los Angeles, Las Vegas, the Netherlands, and Japan, specifically in Okinawa and Nagoya. What surprises many is his execution speed, which never compromises quality. Where many tattoo artists require two or more sessions to complete a complex piece, Marco often finishes it in just one. This offers a real benefit to clients: high-level results, more efficiently delivered, and with reduced time and cost without ever sacrificing detail or integrity. His artistic identity is firmly rooted in black-and-grey realism, but it's the Chicano influence that gives his work its distinctive soul: expressive faces, religious iconography, and symbol-rich imagery. This influence is not superficial or adopted lightly, it stems from extended collaborations in California, especially in Los Angeles, where Marco immersed himself in the cultural and visual language of this genre. It's not imitation, but genuine assimilation, developed over time and guided by deep respect for its origins. Today, Marco Inkman is a member of the international Emalla collective, a group that brings together some of the most skilled artists in realism from around the world. Despite growing recognition, Marco remains grounded, professional, and fully dedicated to his craft.
